findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution available along the main cookline. Discussed with the PIC and a sani bucket was prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer solution present if food preparation, food handling, or service is occurring to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The hood baffles of the ventilation system above the fryers were observed accumulated with dried grease debris. The sticker on the side of the system indicates that M&R cleaning professionals cleans the hood system, however, the last service date reads December 2025. The baffles can be cleaned manually in house by employees. See that a professional hood service company cleans the internal duct work routinely to prevent debris accumualtion.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the potato cutter to be accumulated with dried food debris. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure that the cutter is cleaned after every use to prevent debris accumulation and possible contamination of foods items.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The ice shoots of the soda machine were observed soiled with black and pinkish debris. Shown and discussed with the PIC. The facility mentioned that the ice shoots will be cleaned in the near future. Suggested contacting the manufacturing company to service internal work. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation. Will schedule an additional follow-up for April 23, 2026.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The two storage racks inside of the walk in cooler still contained visible mold on the surfaces.  A presence of mold inside of any cold holding equipment poses several health risks to food items, as well as food contact surfaces. The employees cleaned the racks prior to the visit, however, mold was still observed on surfaces. Ensure that shelves are taken outdoors and are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold buildup up.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink along the cooking line was not observed leaking, however, there has been a repeated history of the bottom pipe leaking water. During the April 4th routine inspection, waste water was observed leaking from the pipe, but the PIC tightened the pipe to stop the leak as a temporary fix. The sink is also being supported by a 2x4 wood plank. Will schedule an additional followup for 4/23/2026 to ensure that the sink has been completely repaired.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There weren’t any handwashing signs posted at the handwashing sinks in each of the bathrooms. A handwashing sign instructing employees to wash hands before returning to work after a bathroom break should be posted and available in bathrooms. A sign for each bathroom was given to the PIC to post. Ensure that handwashing signs are posted and available for employees.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: There was mold starting to form on the lid of a container storing a food item (maybe icing). The container was shown to the PIC. There was also a significant amount of mold buildup on the shelves inside of the walk in cooler - see violation #49 for further details. A follow-up to ensure that the shelves, food items, and food packaging are in good condition and are free of mold.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

The facility mentioned that the ice shoots will be cleaned in the near future. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation. Will follow-up on 4/13/2026.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The two storage racks inside of the walk in cooler were observed HEAVILY accumulated with mold buildup. Shown and discussed with the PIC. The facility has a plan to deep clean on a day that the facility isn’t in operation. A presence of mold inside of any cold holding equipment poses several health risks to food items, as well as food contact surfaces. Ensure that shelves are taken outdoors and are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold buildup up.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There was a leak coming from the pipe underneath the handwashing sink in the kitchen area. The sink is also being supported by a 2x4 wood plank. The PIC tighten the piping during the inspection as a temporary fix. Because this was also a violation at the July 2025 routine inspection, a follow-up is being scheduled for 4/13/2026 to ensure that the plumbing is repaired by a licensed plumber and is in leakfree condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility is in need of a detail cleaning in many areas of the store - including floors, walls, and ceilings of the cook-line, floors and walls in the back stock area, and underneath and behind large pieces of equipment. Pieces of equipment that aren't stationary shall be pulled from wall so that floors and walls can be thoroughly cleaned. The PIC mentioned that the facility has a plan to deep the facility maybe on a day that the facility isn't in operation. In the meantime, be sure to thoroughly clean the facility during down time to prevent the buildup of splatter, food, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink along the cookline is starting to pull from the wall and has about an 1/2 inch gap between the wall and the sink. This gap allows for unwanted debris to fall and accumulate behind the sink. Ensure that the sink is caulked to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was dried food debris in the basin of the kitchen’s handwashing sink. Discussed with person-in-charge (PIC) that hand sinks are to only be used for handwashing purposes. Ensure hand sinks are never used for warewashing or as a dump sink. Be sure to educate employees on proper use of handsinks.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There are several insect devices that are located directly above food prep areas. There is a hanging glue trap (with many dead flies) placed above the prep cooler along the cookline. Discussed moving the trap further from the prep cooler or an area where food prep doesn’t occur. There is also a sticky trap stored near a holding rack where fried chicken is dumped after being fried. The PIC mentioned that Plunkett’s, the facility’s pest control company, placed the trap in that specific area. Discussed that insect traps are to never be stored in a manner where it can contaminate food or food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: There are at least three baking sheet pans used to catch leaking blood from raw animal protein. These sheets are placed underneath storage racks inside of the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC that sheets are to be replaced at the end of each night if soiled with animal liquids. Ensure that sheet pans are cleaned at a frequency to preclude accumulation and unwanted odors.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility is in need of a detail cleaning in many areas of the store - including floors, walls, and ceilings of the cook-line and the bakery area, floor of the walk in cooler, floors and walls in the back stock area, and underneath and behind large pieces of equipment. PIC mentioned that the facility is in the process of a transition and that they are planning to perform a deep cleaning soon. In the meantime, be sure to thoroughly clean the facility during down time to prevent the buildup of splatter and food debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: None of the employees working at the time of the inspection were Certified Food Protection Managers. Ensure that there is always at least one certified food protection manager present during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off the faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing techniques. To avoid recontaminating freshly washed hands, be sure to use a barrier when operating faucet handles after washing hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were several packages of hot dogs in the walk in cooler that lacked proper date marking. PIC mentioned that the facility rarely prepares hot dogs. Discussed that any TCS food item held in house for longer than 24 hours must bear date marking and be used within 7 days of opening.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: There was an accumulation of mold buildup on the door-seal of the prep cooler along the cook-line. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent mold buildup and possible contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn't any paper towels located at the handwashing in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided to the dispenser. Be sure that paper towels are available at every handwashing sink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: A slight accumulation of mold was observed on the inside surface of the ice shoot. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the ice shoot is cleaned as often as necessary to avoid mold accumulation and possible contamination of ice.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soda nozzles on the soda machine were observed to be soiled. Discussed with PIC and nozzles were cleaned with a sani towel. Ensure that soda nozzles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil build-up. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
